editorial:
Imagine giving up your dream spot at MIT just to look after your younger siblings after a terrible car crash. That is exactly where you find Ethan, a guy crushed by guilt who is trying to keep his family together. He is working on a wild science project to bring his parents back, but things go sideways fast. You will feel the tension as the house starts feeling less like a home and more like a trap. It is a slow burn that mixes family drama with some really creepy supernatural stuff, making you wonder if Ethan is losing his mind or if something truly evil has moved in.

The acting is solid and the twists keep you guessing until the very end. While some parts of the plot feel a bit confusing, the scares are effective and the mood is spot on. If you like stories about grief and ghost stories, you should definitely give this one a shot. It is a great pick for a rainy night when you want something that feels a bit different from your usual jump-scare movies.
endingExplained: You find out that Ethan's experiment actually worked, but it brought back something wrong. The entity pretending to be his parents is actually a monster that feeds on grief. In the end, the creature tries to take over completely. Ethan has to face the truth that his parents are gone for good. He eventually destroys the machine and the entity, accepting his loss so he can finally move on with his siblings.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves sci-fi horror and twist endings.
